# Why separate responsibility from attention?

The current Focus skill selects a role. Testing it in an established Architecture chat switched that chat to Purpose.
The user then requested protection for specialist continuity and identified Data and Security as concerns shared across roles.

![Current role replacement compared with a stable role and temporary concern.](images/options.svg)

## Actual baseline

The [Focus workflow](../../../skills/asdg-focus/SKILL.md) handles free-text role selection and ambiguity, but has no concern model.
Its [session policy](../../../skills/asdg-focus/session-policy.md) retains one role per conversation and forbids activation by mere mention.
The [Decision extension contract](../../../skills/asdg-decision/specialization.md) already supports optional role-local enrichment.
A separate Purpose chat was found and opened during this conversation. That demonstrates navigation, not an implemented routing policy.
The warning before a cross-role switch was applied conversationally; it is not yet saved in the skill.

## Alternatives

| Option | Benefit | Cost and limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Keep role-only Focus](10-option-role-only.md) | Minimal change; ordinary prompts can discuss concerns. | Concern context and return behavior remain informal. |
| [Concern-specific role grid](11-option-specialist-grid.md) | Explicit isolated mandates. | Duplicated knowledge, menu clutter and fragmented ownership. |
| [Compose role and concern](12-option-composition.md) | Stable responsibility; shared concern knowledge; sparse specialization. | Requires explicit context resolution and conflict handling. |

Recommend composition, retaining ordinary conversation for lightweight questions.
This is a design judgment grounded in the user's workflow, not a measured productivity result.
Separate chats and subagents are execution arrangements available to the design; they are not competing definitions of Concern.

## Consequences and revisit conditions

The shared library needs an owner and review discipline; loading every concern for every task would waste attention and tokens.
Focus must report which role remains responsible and must not hide relevant consequences outside the selected concern.
Start with three concerns and two roles; extend only where real tasks reveal recurring guidance.
Reconsider the design if the pilot produces silent role switches, duplicated guidance, confusing return behavior or more ceremony than useful evidence.
If concern knowledge never needs to be retained between turns, role-only Focus may be sufficient.
If legal or organizational accountability demands an independently owned specialist function, propose a real role explicitly instead of treating it as a concern mode.

# Twelve concerns in plain language

A concern is something that matters to the outcome. It can be a subject, a desired quality or a business obligation.
The twelve entries are a starting vocabulary, not twelve gates or mandatory checklists.

![Different roles ask different questions about a shared concern.](images/perspectives.svg)

| Concern | Main question | Stable proposed ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Value & Cost | Is it worthwhile, and what does it cost to build, run and change? | value-cost |
| People & Experience | Can people understand, access and use it effectively? | people-experience |
| Data | Is the information accurate, useful and well managed? | data |
| Security | Are we protected against unauthorized access and misuse? | security |
| Privacy | Are we respecting people's information, choices and expectations? | privacy |
| Reliability & Recovery | Can people depend on it when things go wrong? | reliability-recovery |
| Speed & Capacity | Is it fast enough, and can it handle demand? | speed-capacity |
| Integration | Does it work with the other systems we need? | integration |
| Operations & Visibility | Can we run it, see what is happening and resolve problems? | operations-visibility |
| Change & Adaptability | Can it evolve as needs and dependencies change? | change-adaptability |
| Compliance & Accountability | Can we meet obligations and show who is responsible? | compliance-accountability |
| Safety & Human Control | Can we avoid harm and preserve appropriate human control? | safety-human-control |

## Boundaries without artificial silos

Security addresses unauthorized actions; Privacy addresses appropriate use even by authorized actors.
Data covers meaning, quality, ownership and lifecycle; its confidentiality or recovery needs connect to other concerns.
Reliability concerns dependable outcomes; Operations concerns the ability to run and investigate the system.
Cost includes money, time, effort and future change. “Focus on Cost” resolves directly to the cost aspect of Value & Cost.
AI accuracy, uncertainty and autonomy belong to relevant concerns rather than requiring a thirteenth AI category.
Compute, databases and messaging are useful topics within a task; they need not become top-level concerns.

## Library rules

Each concern defines its purpose, aliases, common questions, relevant evidence, overlaps and typical trade-offs.
Use stable words for IDs; display order is not a lifecycle number. “05” continues to mean Architecture, never Privacy.
Local terminology may refine an existing concern. Create a new concern only when recurring needs cannot be expressed clearly with the existing vocabulary.
Governance maintains shared definitions through authorized methodology changes, informed by specialist experience.
A concern never owns the entire project or authorizes actions; the active role remains responsible.

# Focus should preserve the conversation's owner

Interpret the user's whole request against the current role, task and concern. A word match alone is insufficient.
The following behavior is proposed; the current skill still implements role selection only.

![Interpret a request, distinguish concern from role, and preserve state until a choice is resolved.](images/routing.svg)

| Situation | Proposed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| New chat: “focus on architecture” | Load 05, activate it, then report the role. |
| New chat: “focus on Data” | Record a pending concern and ask which responsibility is needed; do not infer Architecture. |
| Architecture: “focus on Data” | Keep 05, load Data guidance, announce the temporary focus. |
| Architecture: “how much will this cost?” | Answer using Cost; do not silently change persistent focus from an ordinary question. |
| Architecture: “focus on business intent” | Resolve Purpose; offer separate Purpose chat, switch here, or keep Architecture. |
| Architecture: “switch this chat to Purpose; keep its history” | Explicit informed reassignment is sufficient; do not ask again. |
| “Back to overall architecture” | Clear concern focus; retain 05 and the task. |
| “Clear role / return to general assistant” | Clear role and concern after an explicit request. |
| “Back” with several plausible meanings | Ask whether to restore previous concern or return to the role's overall view. |
| Quoted examples or explaining Focus | Discuss only; do not activate or change anything. |

## Choosing without clutter

A bare Focus invocation in an unfocused chat offers twelve selectable roles with Governance separately.
In a focused chat, offer overall view, choose a concern, or change role; accept free text throughout.
If a role is already known and no concern can be resolved, offer the twelve selectable concerns.
For real ambiguity, show only plausible interpretations, a recommendation with a reason, and alternatives.
If the client cannot display twelve options accessibly, present a compact fallback list; never silently truncate choices.
A preselected choice, timeout or praise is not an answer.

## Protecting existing chats

Before a cross-role change, recommend reusing an existing specialist chat; create one only when explicitly selected and no suitable chat is confirmed.
The current role, focus and title remain intact until the user chooses a destination or reassignment.
Opening a chat is navigation; sending it a task or context is a separate action requiring authorization.
“Go back to 05” immediately after an accidental switch is an explicit restoration request, not another onboarding interview.
Keep the public entry as ASDG focus. Document the distinction so existing numeric role shortcuts remain usable.

# One method, enriched by role and concern

A Skill is a reusable method. Its interface accepts the task and context; optional guidance deepens its application.
This extends the existing Decision enrichment pattern without creating a skill for every role-concern pair.

![A shared method combines role and concern guidance inside unchanged authority boundaries.](images/composition.svg)

## Proposed loading contract

1. Resolve the role through the existing role catalogue and concerns through a new shared concern index.
2. Read the role contract and the shared skill's required sources before performing work.
3. Load the role-local method when present, using the existing Decision path.
4. Load the selected concern's shared guidance once.
5. Load a role-local concern supplement when present; absence means use shared guidance.
6. Apply the method and return its normal result with relevant concern evidence and trade-offs.

| Proposed source | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Existing `asdg/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | Shared workflow and output contract. |
| Existing `<role>/skills/decision/SKILL.md` | Optional architectural, evaluation or other role criteria. |
| New `asdg/concerns/catalog.json` | Stable IDs, aliases and canonical paths. |
| New `asdg/concerns/<id>/README.md` | Shared concern knowledge, questions and evidence. |
| Optional `<role>/concerns/<id>.md` | Only meaningful differences for this role. |

These are proposed source paths, not created runtime packages.
Concern guides are knowledge resources, not public skills or agents. Local supplements need no discovery adapter.
Do not create 144 empty role-concern files or a third skill-by-role-by-concern directory hierarchy.
A supplement can contain a short Decision-specific section if experience justifies it.

## Composition and conflict rules

The role contract, shared method obligations and runtime permissions remain binding.
Concern guidance can add questions, criteria and explanatory views; it cannot remove evidence requirements or widen authority.
A local supplement may refine generic advice, identifying the reason and context. Contradictory requirements must be surfaced, not resolved by “last file wins.”
Absent optional guidance uses the generic method. Present but unreadable or invalid guidance produces a named gap, not silent fallback.
Unrelated work may continue; do not claim the missing specialization was applied.
Resolve paths from catalogues and trusted repository definitions, never by concatenating arbitrary user text.
Do not recursively invoke shared and local skills; track sources already loaded.

## Applying existing skills

Decision returns the same rationale, alternatives, evidence, choice status, consequences and revisit conditions, now noting relevant concerns.
Role explains stable responsibility and current attention separately. Status reports both; Suggestion uses both without changing them.
Concern focus does not require a saved decision for every answer. Save material assigned decisions under the existing owning contract.

# Retain role and focus separately

The session needs a small conversation-local context, not a shared global “active specialist” file.
A concern change is reversible attention; a role change is a responsibility transition.

![Concern focus changes within one role; separate reassignment changes the role only after a deliberate choice.](images/session.svg)

## Proposed context fields

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| project | Verified project binding; unknown stays unknown. |
| role | One selected catalogue role, None, or Unknown if recovery evidence is lost. |
| concern_focus | Zero or more selected concern IDs, with one primary concern when useful. |
| task_scope | The current question, deliverable, subject and limits. |
| previous_focus | One prior concern set and scope for explicit return; no unbounded focus stack. |
| activation_receipt | User request, resolved role/concerns, source paths and versions actually read. |
| pending_choice | Unresolved candidate or destination; does not replace active context. |
| integration_owner | Who combines findings when work is split; absent for ordinary solo work. |

Allow multiple concerns when requested, such as “Cost and Reliability”; recommend one or two for clarity rather than enforce an arbitrary hard limit.
A narrow focus increases depth, not permission to ignore consequential effects elsewhere.
“Overall architecture” clears concern_focus. “Previous focus” restores the saved concern set after checking its guidance.
A new role assignment clears old role-specific focus by default; retain a concern only when the user's request makes that intent clear.

## Lifecycle and failure handling

Read and validate required guidance before committing a transition. Failed loading leaves prior role, concern and title intact.
A rename failure leaves a successfully activated context intact and is reported separately.
Keep the base title role-based; optionally add the concern suffix after activation, such as “05 Architecture · Data — Speaker Coach.”
The title is presentation, never proof of activation or authority.
Retain the receipt during compaction. If role history is lost, report Unknown and ask for reaffirmation; never infer it from filenames or a title.
If only concern history is lost, retain the verified role and ask which focus to resume.
On changed guidance, reload relevant sources and disclose material changes before relying on previous conclusions.

## Authority and persistence

Focus creates no implementation, approval, deployment, messaging or delegation authority.
Keep active context in this chat. Durable deliverables reference concerns but do not become a second lifecycle or sprint state store.
A future optional team directory could map roles to chats; it must verify current native state and handle stale or duplicate entries.
Do not introduce that directory during the first pilot; use native discovery with explicit limitations.

# One role can have several focused investigators

Start with one agent when sequential attention is sufficient. Split work only when the expected insight justifies coordination cost.
The general architect remains responsible for integrating architectural findings.

![A general architect sends a bounded Data question to an investigator and integrates its evidence on return.](images/collaboration.svg)

| Arrangement | Use when | Continuity and control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same chat, temporary concern | The user wants deeper examination now. | Same role, history and owner; return to overall view afterward. |
| Separate user-owned chat | The user wants an enduring parallel workspace. | Explicit creation or reuse; pass only authorized context and assignments. |
| Bounded subagent | An explicitly authorized delegated investigation can proceed independently. | Parent retains integration; child returns findings through its supported channel. |

An explicitly requested second architect can have role 05 and focus Data without replacing the first architect.
A concern does not create a new ASDG role ID or imply a new person with approval authority.
Existing project permissions and delegation restrictions apply to every participant.

## Minimum investigation brief

State the project, role, concern, question, source baseline, output expected, allowed actions, exclusions, and integration owner.
Pass relevant decisions and uncertainties with provenance; distinguish accepted choices from proposed documents.
Use the smallest sufficient source set. A fresh chat does not inherit this conversation automatically.
For read-only work, say so explicitly. If writes are separately authorized, allocate nonoverlapping files and preserve other contributors' edits.
Agree a stopping condition: return the bounded answer and evidence, not an expanding autonomous research programme.

## Return and synthesis

Return findings, alternatives, evidence, confidence limits, affected concerns and unresolved trade-offs.
The parent checks source freshness and conflicting assumptions before incorporating findings into the authoritative decision.
A Data investigator may recommend retention that conflicts with Privacy or Cost. The integrating architect explains the conflict and the human decides consequential trade-offs.
An investigator's recommendation is not a parent decision, user approval or proof of independent review.
If the investigator fails, report the unanswered question; partial work does not become complete evidence.

## Routing safeguards

Match project and verified role before reusing a chat; inspect candidates rather than trusting titles alone.
Limited inventory is not proof that no chat exists. Ask or provide a manual route if a suitable existing chat cannot be resolved.
Avoid duplicate creation after uncertain tool results. Report created, activated, assigned and completed as separate outcomes.
Opening an existing chat needs no work message. Sending a brief requires explicit authorization; authorization is not implied by a concern selection.

# The same concern changes meaning across roles

Cost illustrates why concerns should cross the lifecycle. Each role produces evidence appropriate to its responsibility.
The specialist contract still determines whether that contribution is an assessment, proposal or authorized delivery.

![Shared Cost concern connects business outcomes, design trade-offs, test evidence and operational observations.](images/perspectives.svg)

| Role | Cost question | Typical contribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 Context | Who pays, who spends time, and what constraints exist? | Stakeholder and cost-context evidence. |
| 02 Purpose | Which benefits justify the expense? | Desired value, affordability and non-goals. |
| 03 Use Cases | Which interactions create workload or user effort? | Scenarios and demand assumptions. |
| 04 Evaluation | How should alternatives be compared fairly? | Measurement protocol and comparable cost basis. |
| 05 Architecture | Which boundaries and dependencies drive lifetime cost? | Trade-offs, assumptions and revisit triggers. |
| 06 POC | Which uncertain cost driver needs an experiment? | Bounded feasibility evidence. |
| 07 Planning | What effort, dependencies and budget affect sequencing? | Scoped work and explicit estimates. |
| 08 Detailed Design | Which interface behaviors create unnecessary work? | Contracts for batching, retries and resource limits. |
| 09 Build & Test | Does implementation behave within the agreed limits? | Observations from authorized implementation and tests. |
| 10 Review & Release | Is cost evidence sufficient for this candidate? | Readiness findings and unresolved risks. |
| 11 Operations | What does it actually cost to run and recover? | Usage, support and operational evidence. |
| 12 Insights | What patterns suggest improvement? | Learning and candidate improvements. |

Governance coordinates ownership and cross-role conflicts; it does not become the owner of every cost calculation.

## Other concerns follow the same pattern

For Security, Purpose identifies protection expectations; Architecture defines trust boundaries; Evaluation defines attack and misuse tests; Operations examines access and incidents.
For Data, Purpose identifies useful information; Use Cases models its meaning; Architecture allocates ownership; Operations examines retention and recovery.
The same source may inform several roles, but each should add its own evidence or reasoning rather than copy the same checklist.
Concerns do not reorder lifecycle stages or require all stages to run for each question.

## Keeping the library small

Start with shared Data, Security and Value & Cost guidance, plus demonstrated role-local needs.
Compare Architecture and Purpose in the first pilot; add Evaluation and Operations after the interface proves useful.
Do not claim to cover all twelve concerns just because their names appear in a catalogue.
Measure usefulness through clearer questions, preserved ownership and reviewable evidence, not document or agent counts.

# Worked example: focus on Cost

Scenario: the Speaker Coach architect is assessing a local service connected to a cloud model for live interview assistance.
This example illustrates the proposed method; it does not reopen the selected SDK decision or claim measured costs.

![Compare total cost across build, live use, operations and future change against the desired benefit.](images/cost.svg)

## A useful conversation

User: “Focus on Cost for the live meeting architecture.”
Assistant: “Still 05 Architecture. I will examine build, runtime, operational and change costs for this meeting flow.”
The task remains architecture evaluation. Purpose owns the value judgment; Evaluation can define measurements; Operations supplies actual running costs.

## Frame the decision before calculating

Use a declared workload: meeting length, sessions per month, concurrent users, audio handling, model input/output, retention and expected retries.
Distinguish one-time effort from recurring costs, user effort from provider charges, and cash expenses from uncertain opportunity costs.
A planning expression is:
**Total cost = build effort + usage charges + storage/network + operation/support + expected change and recovery effort.**
Keep each term's unit and horizon explicit; use ranges or “unknown” instead of adding incompatible quantities or inventing precision.
Do not treat a user's existing laptop or an engineer's time as free; explain whether the comparison uses incremental cash or full economic cost.
Provider rates would need dated primary-source verification during a real assessment; this proposal makes no pricing claim.

## Compare credible scenarios

| Scenario | Main trade-off | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every transcript update triggers reasoning | Frequent opportunities for advice; potentially more work. | Calls per minute, useful updates, latency and usage. |
| Reason only on meaningful conversation events | Potentially less work; may delay or miss useful guidance. | Event recall, advice timeliness and measured usage. |
| Local preprocessing before cloud reasoning | Potentially less transmitted content; local complexity and maintenance. | Reduction achieved, quality impact, resource use and support effort. |

These are illustrative candidates, not authorized changes or benchmark winners.
Check Privacy, Reliability and Speed before recommending a cheaper design: cost reduction is not success if it undermines the purpose.
Define an observation that could reverse the recommendation, such as missed advice, unacceptable latency or materially higher operating effort.

## Result and return

A Decision result states assumptions, comparable options, known evidence, unknown costs and a proposed choice with revisit triggers.
“Return to overall architecture” removes the Cost focus; its findings remain linked to the architectural decision.
Only assigned documentation creates a package. A conversational estimate stays conversational unless the user asks to save it.

# Adopt the model through a bounded pilot

Recommended implementation order below is a proposal, not an active sprint or permission to modify operational policies.
Each increment should leave the existing role catalogue and approved client artifacts usable.

![Review the model, pilot three concerns, validate skill composition, then consider parallel work.](images/adoption.svg)

| Increment | Proposed changes | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Agree the contract | Review vocabulary, role-switch safeguard, clearing semantics and ownership. | Explicit decision on these behaviors. |
| 2. Pilot concern focus | Add shared index and Data/Security/Cost guides; update Focus, session policy and tests. | Correct same-chat transitions and no silent role changes. |
| 3. Compose skills | Enrich Decision, Role, Status and Suggestion; add only needed role supplements. | Shared method outputs remain valid across Architecture and Purpose. |
| 4. Integrate team routing | Align Create team, native role adapters, templates and installation checks. | Reuse, creation and navigation outcomes verified in the app. |
| 5. Trial parallel attention | One authorized Data investigation with a general architect integrating. | Bounded brief, preserved ownership and evidence-based synthesis. |
| 6. Expand deliberately | Add concern guides and roles where recurring use justifies them. | Demonstrated value and manageable guidance size. |

## Behavior acceptance cases

| Given / request | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Unfocused / “Data” | Ask role; no fabricated architect selection. |
| Architecture / “focus on cost” | Role remains 05; Value & Cost focus activated after reads. |
| Purpose / “focus on security” | Purpose questions about protection outcomes, not design implementation. |
| Architecture / “how much does it cost?” | Relevant answer; no persistent focus transition. |
| Architecture / “business intent” as Focus request | Offer separate Purpose chat or deliberate reassignment. |
| Architecture / explicit informed switch | Switch once; no redundant confirmation. |
| Data focus / “overall architecture” | Clear concern; retain role and task. |
| Any role / quoted focus example | No context mutation. |
| Pending selection / timeout | Existing context and title remain. |
| Missing optional supplement | Generic role-plus-concern method works. |
| Invalid existing supplement | Named gap; no silent claim of successful specialization. |
| Concern suggests wider permissions | Preserve role and runtime boundaries. |
| Resume with lost receipt | Report unknown context; ask only for missing selection. |
| Existing chat not in limited inventory | Do not claim absence or create an automatic duplicate. |
| Authorized second architect / Data | Parent stays general; child has bounded scope; findings return for integration. |
| Concern-specific choice / conflicting evidence | Surface affected concerns and unresolved human decision. |

## Migration and evaluation

Keep numeric role shortcuts and the single public Focus adapter. Register no public concern-specific skills.
Existing chat receipts retain their role and start with no concern; do not mass-rename or message the team.
Preserve existing decision paths and hashes; add concern context only when an artifact is actually revised.
Run source/link/structure tests, isolated semantic exercises, then live picker, retention, switching and recovery checks.
Source tests alone cannot establish native behavior. Record task success, clarification burden, unwanted switches and guidance size without inventing numeric thresholds.
Roll back pilot behavior by reverting its bounded source changes, retaining review history and client evidence; explain how active concern contexts return to overall role view.

# Alternative: keep role-only Focus

Continue using Focus exclusively to choose a lifecycle role; discuss Data, Security and Cost through ordinary prompts.

![Role-only Focus replaces the selected role; concern attention stays informal.](images/options.svg)

## Fit and benefits

This is closest to the current implementation and has the lowest migration cost.
It is sufficient if concern questions are brief and do not require retained guidance or reliable return behavior.
Add a warning before role changes and the immediate team-continuity problem is reduced.

## Limitations

There is no explicit concern context for Decision, Status or Suggestion to consume.
Different roles may repeatedly invent the same concern guidance.
“Return to general” and “go back” remain easy to confuse with clearing the role.
Parallel specialists can still work, but their concerns are expressed only in individual assignments.

## Recommendation

Keep ordinary concern questions lightweight, but do not use this as the sole long-term model.
Reconsider it if the composition pilot adds more clarification and source loading than useful continuity.
Its behavior remains a valuable fallback when concern guidance is unavailable and the user chooses a general analysis.

# Alternative: define a role for every concern combination

Create explicit specialist identities such as Architecture–Data, Architecture–Security and Operations–Data.

![A role-by-concern grid multiplies packages and ownership boundaries.](images/grid.svg)

## Fit and benefits

Dedicated identities make sense when there is a genuinely separate mandate, accountable owner or independently governed delivery function.
They may provide stronger isolation for specialized work, although instructions alone do not prove runtime enforcement.

## Costs and failure modes

Twelve roles multiplied by twelve concerns would suggest 144 combinations before methods, project context or governance.
That is an illustrative upper bound on a full grid, not a proposal to create those agents.
Most packages would duplicate role duties, concern knowledge or both; changes could drift across copies.
Users would face a larger picker and uncertain ownership when several combinations describe the same task.
A focus change could repeatedly change identity or create another chat.

## Recommendation

Do not make concern combinations new canonical ASDG roles by default.
Allow multiple instances of an existing role with explicit concerns when the user wants parallel work.
Propose a genuinely new role through governance only when its separate responsibility cannot be represented by a task and concern.

# Recommended: compose role, concern and method

Keep the existing role catalogue. Add shared concern knowledge and a conversation-local focus that reusable skills can consume.

![Shared method, role guidance and selected concern guidance produce one accountable result.](images/composition.svg)

## Why this fits

It preserves the specialist's responsibility while supporting temporary depth.
The same Data guide can help Purpose, Architecture, Evaluation and Operations, with sparse local enrichments.
The existing Decision dispatch pattern offers a concrete starting point: shared interface, optional context-specific guidance.
One public Focus entry supports both familiar role selection and temporary concern attention.

## Costs and controls

Resolution becomes more sophisticated: a phrase may describe a role, concern, task or destination.
Expose the interpretation and ask only when it materially changes responsibility or leaves genuine ambiguity.
Loading too much guidance can reduce usefulness; load selected concerns and necessary overlaps, not the whole library.
Knowledge can conflict; retain authority boundaries, surface incompatible requirements and explain local refinements.
Parallel work adds coordination cost; start with a single agent and explicitly authorized bounded experiments.

## Proposed selection and revisit

Recommend this option for a Data/Security/Cost pilot with Architecture and Purpose.
The user has endorsed the vocabulary, not yet this complete implementation contract.
Revisit after observable pilot evidence: reliable role retention, useful specialization, manageable clarification and preserved authority.
Do not claim success from directory structure, passing syntax checks or this proposal's completion.

# Roles, Concerns, Focus and Skills
Proposal for ASDG methodology • 27 October 2026 • not an implemented workflow or accepted decision.

ASDG should let a person ask “look at Cost” without losing the specialist responsible for the work.
Keep the role stable, share concern knowledge across roles, and use Focus to direct attention temporarily.
Skills remain reusable methods that apply the current role, concern and task context.

![Role remains stable while Focus selects a Concern and a Skill produces evidence.](images/model.svg)

## Recommended direction

**Role is responsibility. Concern is what matters. Focus is current attention. Skill is how we do the work.**
A chat hosts a conversation; an agent performs work. Neither is a new lifecycle stage.
An architect examining Data remains an architect. A second architect may investigate Data while the first integrates the overall design.
Use one public Focus skill, a small shared concern library and optional local enrichments. Avoid a role-by-concern menu or a new agent for every concern.
Begin with same-chat focus. Introduce parallel investigation only when useful and explicitly authorized.

## Decision for tomorrow

The user endorsed the vocabulary and asked for a complete strategy; the mechanisms below remain recommendations.
Review the separation of role and concern, the switching safeguard, and the initial Data/Security/Cost pilot.
No runtime skill, role catalogue, team chat, application behavior or lifecycle approval is changed by this proposal.
Evidence and review limits are recorded in [the review report](../../../../docs/asdg/07-planning/02.6-review-concern-strategy.md).

# Review of the Roles, Concerns and Focus proposal

Prepared 27 October 2026 for the user's request to develop a complete strategy while preserving the existing team context.
Subject: ASDG methodology design, not a new Speaker Coach application feature or an implemented skill change.

![The proposed adoption path moves from agreement through a small pilot to verified composition and selective expansion.](../../../asdg/docs/proposals/roles-concerns-and-focus/images/adoption.svg)

## Delivered proposal

Start with the [strategy overview](../../../asdg/docs/proposals/roles-concerns-and-focus/README.md).
Thirteen short Markdown files explain the model, twelve concerns, Focus behavior, skill composition, session contract, collaboration, lifecycle perspectives, a Cost example, adoption, and three alternatives.
Ten editable SVGs explain relationships and transitions; every substantive document embeds a relevant visual.
The recommendation is stable roles with temporary concern focus, a shared concern library, optional local enrichment and deliberate cross-role transitions.
User endorsement of vocabulary is preserved separately from acceptance of this implementation proposal.

## Evidence and checks

Source inspection covered current Focus, session policy, team creation, Decision specialization, role/runtime contracts and documentation standards.
The prior conversation supplies requirements and observed navigation; it does not prove the proposed concern behavior works.
All thirteen proposal pages rendered in a 720-pixel pane with loaded diagrams at 656 pixels and no page overflow.
All ten distinct diagrams were visually inspected at embedded width; the overview and skill-composition pages were inspected in full.
Comparison and branching diagrams were corrected to avoid implying that alternative choices form a sequence, then rendered and inspected again.
Markdown source limits, local links, SVG XML and exact receipt hashes are checked by the accompanying validation record.
The local structure verifier passed. The broad checker retains eight pre-existing external presentation links in the unchanged methodology README.
The initial sandboxed Chrome launch failed; the same local render succeeded through the approved execution path.

## Limits and integrity

This is an author-reviewed design proposal, not an independent evaluation, runtime test, human acceptance or implementation.
The acceptance scenarios are specified for a future pilot; none is reported as an executed concern-runtime test.
No application tests were rerun because this delivery adds documentation only.
Existing Focus behavior, role catalogue, lifecycle state, sprint state and application files are preserved; selected hashes are recorded in the [technical receipt](02.6-review-concern-strategy.json).
Only new proposal/review files and append-only documentation receipts are part of this delivery; existing unrelated work remains.
No specialist was spawned, no chat was created or messaged, and no commit, push or lifecycle transition was performed.

## Review next

Review the proposed distinction between stable role and temporary focus, the role-change warning, and the Data/Security/Cost pilot.
If selected, implement the first bounded increment and verify the conversational behavior before expanding the library or parallel execution.
